section.form_description: The narrator on their feet in a crowded room, speaking about someone who has died. Sections are the things there are to say about the dead — a habit, a fight, a debt, the once they were wrong, the once they were right when it counted. The tone swings: a story that gets a laugh, a line that lands angry, a stretch that can barely be got through. What holds it together is that none of it is polite — every word is meant.
section.form_note: Above all a eulogy: every speaker laments his loss, tells how they bonded with him and what they loved about him, and celebrates him. The brief asks for nine people on their feet in one room, each saying what there is to say about the dead man: a eulogy, not a two-voice dialogue. Spine is mixed: Thomas is an original character and not in the corpus, so no event or scene names him; sections anchor on the occasions his notes place him in (the Pragia aftermath, the run-up to Omega-4, Tuchanka, Rannoch, the Citadel shore leave, Grissom, the final push) and the speaker's own record of those. Jack holds the first and last turns (~2,500 words each, long as asked), the other seven run 450-1,000 (Grunt, EDI, James short and blunt; Liara, Joker, Tali fullest). Nine sections is inside the form's 6-14 range. Each turn opens by picking up the one before: Jack's grief to Tali's engine room, Tali's hospital-and-hands to Joker's bad days, Joker's jokes to Liara's late nights, Liara's mother story to Grunt's blunt question, Grunt's kitchen guarding to James's training and banter, James's Hammer glimpse to Wrex, Wrex's speech to EDI's data, EDI's four-leaf-clover tally back to Jack. Alcohol and music run through the turns as the room's furniture (Thomas's disco, pop, rock, rap, metal, folk, gabber, electro, and black-metal playlists, ryncol, the taped-up recipes), not as a section of their own. Canon branch: genophage cured, Wrex leads the krogan, geth-quarian peace (Legion dead), Grunt alive, Thane dead; crew do not know what Shepard chose, and his death is unconfirmed. Thomas's unfinished poems for Jack are private to Jack; the French lines are his to be quoted sparingly and, per memory rules, never verbatim-perfect by anyone but Jack.

required_facts.fact: Some time after being awakened aboard the Normandy, the tank-bred krogan Grunt began suffering violent instability and asked Commander Shepard to take him to Tuchanka so he could earn a place among a true krogan clan. Shepard brought him to the Urdnot camp, where the clan leader agreed that Grunt could attempt the Rite of Passage to join Clan Urdnot. Before the Rite, Gatatog Uvenk, a traditionalist battlemaster and leader of Clan Gatatog, publicly challenged Grunt's legitimacy, denouncing him as a factory-made fake unworthy of clan membership and appealing directly to the Urdnot Shaman, who was annoyed by the interruption. Shepard forced Uvenk to back down by affirming that Shepard's team would stand as Grunt's krantt, either through words or a headbutt; Uvenk withdrew his objection but swore to settle the matter later. Uvenk's attitude depended on who led Clan Urdnot: he openly opposed Urdnot Wrex's reforms as weakness, but was deferential if Urdnot Wreav held power. Grunt undertook the Rite in a ruined arena, striking the Keystone to summon escalating waves of varren and klixen and finally a thresher maw, which he could kill outright or merely survive until the timer expired. Immediately afterward Uvenk arrived by shuttle with several Gatatog Warriors. If Grunt had killed the maw, Uvenk grudgingly acknowledged his strength and offered him in-name-only membership in Clan Gatatog as a trophy to boost Uvenk's own standing; if the maw had only been survived, Uvenk dismissed Grunt as impure. Grunt violently rejected the offer, and the ensuing firefight ended with Uvenk and all his warriors dead. Grunt was formally inducted into Clan Urdnot, gained loyalty to Shepard, and expressed satisfaction at Uvenk's death.

Commander Shepard and the Normandy crew investigate a distress call from the Attican Traverse. A krogan scouting team has gone missing while investigating rumors of activity at a rachni relay beyond Udina's position. The Urdnot clan leader—either Urdnot Wrex or Urdnot Wreav—reports the disappearance, and Shepard travels to the planet Utukku in the Mulla Xul system of the Ninmah Cluster to investigate. Upon arrival, Shepard encounters Aralakh Company, an elite krogan unit. If Grunt survived the suicide mission in Mass Effect 2 and was freed from his tank, he leads Aralakh Company; otherwise, Urdnot Dagg commands the unit. The team descends into tunnels beneath Utukku's surface and discovers the horrifying truth: the Reapers have established a massive rachni breeding operation on the planet. The bodies of krogan scouts litter the tunnels, and the facility is overrun with Reaper-corrupted rachni—Ravagers, Swarmers, and other bioengineered horrors. If the original Rachni Queen from Noveria was spared in Mass Effect 1, the Reapers captured her and now hold her prisoner deep within the facility, forcing her to breed an army of mutated rachni. She has proven resistant to Reaper indoctrination, which is why the Reapers use physical restraints. If the Queen was killed in ME1, the Reapers constructed an artificial "Breeder" queen to serve the same purpose. At the central chamber, Shepard confronts the rachni leader and must make a critical choice: rescue her and provide her support for the war effort, or leave her to die. Per `grunt_fate`: If Shepard chooses to save the original Queen or the Breeder, Aralakh Company stages a suicidal holding action against waves of Ravagers. If Grunt leads the company and survived the suicide mission with loyalty gained, he alone survives the onslaught with severe injuries; otherwise, Aralakh Company is completely wiped out. In the Legendary Edition, saving the rachni results in Aralakh Company not being acquired as a war asset at all. If Shepard leaves the rachni to die, Grunt or Dagg gives the order to retreat immediately, and Aralakh Company escapes intact, gaining 25 war asset points. Regardless of the choice, Grunt or Dagg breaks through a wall in the cavern and holds off Reaper-modified rachni to cover Shepard's squad's escape to the shuttle.

canon.statement: In the first weeks after the war, Shepard's death is not confirmed to the crew. Anderson never saw him on the station. The Normandy crash-landed, there's been no word, and the crew takes that silence to mean he's dead: there's no body and no report. After a few months, Shepard is held to be dead by everyone, the crew included: the rubble has been cleared, what the Crucible did is better understood, and there was nowhere on the station he could have escaped to. There is still no body, so no burial. Shepard's lover puts his name on the Normandy's memorial wall, or chooses not to, and the crew holds a night of remembrance for him: to celebrate the man he was, to mourn him, or both.

beats.text: C-Sec emails Shepard about a troublemaking krogan and asks the Commander to report to the officer on patrol on the Silversun Strip. Shepard finds Grunt detained at a noodle stand and politely muscles C-Sec off his back before getting the story.
Grunt had been recovering in Huerta Memorial Hospital after the battle on Utukku, and got bored. He was broken out by being lowered on a rope, which did not work — he fell several storeys.
The night went on to the Krogan Memorial statue on the Presidium, which they climbed rather than looked at, taking pictures of themselves on it.
When C-Sec arrived, Grunt threw a bottle of ryncol at their shuttle and set it alight. The pilot jumped clear; Grunt got in and took it for a joyride until he crashed it into a noodle stand.
C-Sec caught up with him while he was buying noodles, because he was hungry. He dropped Shepard's name to avoid the brig — which is why Shepard is standing there at all.
The Krogan Monument itself is a statue of a krogan warrior standing in the lake near the Citadel Tower on the Presidium, commissioned to commemorate the krogan.

scenes.when: 2185, after Horizon, once Grunt is woken from his tank

beats.text: Grunt believes he is seriously ill and asks to be taken to Tuchanka for a diagnosis. Shepard takes it to the leader of Clan Urdnot.

The Urdnot leader explains Grunt is not sick, only of the age to take the Rite of Passage, and sends the party to the clan Shaman. Gatatog Uvenk, a traditionalist from the Urdnot border camp, protests loudly that Grunt is tank-bred and has no right to the Rite, going over the leader's head to appeal directly to the Shaman, who is plainly irritated by him. Shepard makes Uvenk back down — either humbling him with words or answering his insults with a headbutt — by agreeing before the Shaman to serve as Grunt's krantt. Uvenk withdraws his objection but warns he will settle the matter elsewhere.
The Rite runs in three waves, each summoned by striking the keystone. Varren first, in numbers.
Second wave: klixen, fire-breathers, dropped in by harvester.
Third is not a wave. It is a thresher maw, and it is meant to be survived rather than killed — the timer runs five minutes.

The Rite over, a shuttle lands carrying Uvenk and several Gatatog Warriors. Uvenk offers to take Grunt into Clan Gatatog — but only as a trophy and an in-name-only member, to raise Uvenk's own standing. Grunt, his identity, krantt and lineage disrespected, violently rejects the offer, and whatever Shepard says the encounter ends in a firefight. Shepard kills Uvenk and all the Gatatog Warriors. On the Normandy afterward Grunt thanks Shepard and says plainly he is glad Uvenk is dead.

A cut Normandy conversation would have followed if Shepard had ordered Grunt not to speak for himself against Uvenk's offer rather than letting him answer. Grunt, now settled that his place as a krogan is real, tells Shepard he liked the Rite but still has a problem: making that decision for him "was going too far," and if Shepard cannot trust him with Uvenk's clumsy offer, will there be a gun at his back against the Collectors? Unless Shepard takes a hard line, Grunt gets annoyed at every excuse offered — "get consistent, Shepard... maybe I start thinking someone else should lead" — though his loyalty is never actually at risk.

evidence.text:
Grunt was a genetically engineered krogan super soldier, bred and educated in a tank on Korlus by the krogan warlord Okeer. Okeer had once sought a cure for the genophage but grew disillusioned, believing it had reduced krogan identity to mere survival, and instead pursued a genetically perfect warrior. With Collector assistance he rejected thousands of flawed specimens before producing his ideal prototype, whose genome incorporated traits from renowned krogan including Shiagur, Kredak, Moro, Terg, Wrend, and Veeoll. Okeer died from toxins released by the Blue Suns mercenary Jedore, and Commander Shepard, who had come to recruit Okeer, instead took the tank aboard the Normandy SR-2.

When Shepard released him, the newly awakened krogan pinned Shepard to a wall and demanded a name before killing the Commander. He took "Grunt" from one of the last words in Okeer's final message, saying, "It has no meaning. It'll do." Shepard could persuade him to join the mission against the Collectors or shoot him into submission. Lacking a krogan upbringing, Grunt was violent, impulsive, and prone to charging recklessly, but was a formidable asset for his strength and fighting prowess. He harbored doubt over being tank-bred, considering himself weak for being given strength, and often sought Shepard's guidance, calling Shepard "battlemaster" once loyal.

For his loyalty, after Grunt became anxious and irrational, EDI or Kelly Chambers alerted Shepard; the condition was the krogan equivalent of puberty. Shepard took him to Tuchanka and Clan Urdnot, where he completed a Rite of Passage with Shepard as his krantt to earn clan membership.

In Mass Effect 3, provided Grunt was released from his tank and survived the Collector base, he returned commanding Aralakh Company, Clan Urdnot's best unit. He helped Shepard investigate missing squads in the tunnels of Utukku, where they found a brood of rachni twisted by Reaper technology. If Shepard spared the Rachni Queen, Aralakh Company was left to cover her escape and was slaughtered, and Grunt died unless his loyalty had been secured; if Shepard abandoned the queen, Grunt ordered a retreat and survived regardless, limping out asking for food. A survived Grunt contributed to the war effort, sent a drunken misspelled message, and could speak to Shepard on Earth before the final push, thanking the Commander for getting him out of the tank. If Grunt survived, the genophage was cured, and organics and synthetics were not merged, he and a surviving Wrex were welcomed home to Tuchanka as heroes. If he died or was never freed, his role was filled by Urdnot Dagg. In the Citadel DLC, Grunt was detained by C-Sec after a drunken rampage, could fight in the Armax Arsenal Arena, and appeared at Shepard's party. Steve Blum voiced Grunt.

Okeer's Legacy on Korlus. 2185, after Freedom's Progress Jedore's Blue Suns camp and Okeer's cloning lab on Korlus; then the Normandy Okeer reveals he has been mass-producing and flash-indoctrinating tank-bred krogan in search of the "perfect" specimen, handing his rejects to Jedore as an army she cannot command, and wants to trade his Collector knowledge for escape. Jedore announces over the PA that Okeer released the krogan without authorisation and begins pumping krogan-killing gas into the facility; Okeer stays behind to protect the tank holding his legacy.

"Dossier: The Warlord" was a Mass Effect 2 recruitment mission, available after Freedom's Progress as part of the Illusive Man's first set of dossiers. Dr. Okeer was described as a brilliant, brutal krogan warlord who had fought in the Krogan Rebellions, become obsessed with saving the krogan from the genophage, and was believed to have contacted the Collectors for technology to that end. He was operating from a Blue Suns camp on Korlus commanded by Jedore.

Fighting through Blue Suns forces (Troopers, Legionnaires, Centurions, and rocket-firing Heavies), Shepard's squad encountered a "Tank-Grown Krogan," only seven days old, one of Okeer's many rejected creations. He opened a path into the research base but would not accompany the squad. Inside, if Shepard had spared Rana Thanoptis on Virmire, she appeared and fled, saying she knew how Shepard worked. Okeer revealed he had been mass-producing and flash-indoctrinating tank-bred krogan in search of the "perfect" specimen, supplying his rejects as an army for Jedore, who could not command them. He wanted to bargain his knowledge of the Collectors for escape. Jedore then announced over the PA that Okeer had released the krogan without authorization and began pumping krogan-killing gas into the facility. Okeer chose to stay behind to protect his legacy, the perfect krogan in his tank.

Shepard fought Jedore, who wielded a rocket launcher and a YMIR Mech while tank-bred krogan broke loose around her, and killed her. Returning to the lab, Shepard found Okeer already dead from the toxins; his final recorded words asked Shepard to protect his legacy and admitted he had not known what the Collectors planned for the human colonists. The tank was recovered to the Normandy. Opening it (in the separate mission "Dr. Okeer's Legacy") released Grunt, who slammed Shepard against a wall before being persuaded or forced to back down; impressed by Shepard's strength, he joined the crew. Rewards included platinum and Sniper Rifle Damage and Krogan Vitality upgrades. If Grunt was never released he would not appear in Mass Effect 3; if released and surviving the suicide mission, he later led a krogan commando unit investigating a resurgent rachni. The mission was written by Lukas Kristjanson after a first pass by Brian Kindregan.

*For his gameplay attributes in Mass Effect 2, see Squad Members Guide (Mass Effect 2\)\#Grunt.* Grunt was created on Korlus by the krogan warlord Okeer, who had initially sought a cure for the genophage but became disillusioned with its long\-term effects. Okeer believed that the genophage had reduced krogan identity to a test of survival, weakening the species by rewarding only endurance rather than strength, unity, or vision. Determined to restore the krogan to greatness, he abandoned his cure and instead pursued the creation of a genetically perfect warrior. With assistance from the Collectors, Okeer experimented extensively, rejecting thousands of flawed specimens before producing his ideal prototype. Grunt’s genetic code incorporated traits from renowned krogan—including Shiagur, Kredak, Moro, Terg, Wrend, and Veeoll—making him a living archive of krogan history and strength. After rejecting thousands of specimens as unworthy, Okeer finally produces his perfect prototype before he dies from toxins released by Jedore, a Blue Suns mercenary. Commander Shepard, who had come to Korlus hoping to recruit Okeer, instead recovers the super soldier's tank and takes it aboard the Normandy SR\-2. When Shepard chooses to release the super soldier from his tank, the newly awakened krogan pins Shepard to a wall and declares his intention to kill the Commander, though he desires a name before doing so. He chooses "Grunt", one of the last words in Okeer's final message, claiming, "It has no meaning. It'll do." Shepard either persuades Grunt to join the mission against the Collectors as it will be a good fight for Grunt, or shoots multiple times to subdue him. If Grunt accepts Shepard's offer, he then realizes that Shepard was pointing a gun at him all along, to which Grunt approves. Lacking a proper krogan upbringing, Grunt is both violent and highly unpredictable. He often becomes impatient and charges recklessly into the midst of his foes, (unlike more disciplined krogan fighters like Urdnot Wrex) without Shepard's orders. Despite his unpredictable and violent attitude, he is nonetheless considered a great asset to the mission thanks to his unsurpassed physical strength and fighting prowess. Grunt also harbors personal doubt due to his genetic upbringing, considering himself weak for being given strength compared to the thousands of failures that "at least tried" to become strong on their own. Outside of battle, Grunt often appears naive and particularly enthusiastic about violence and combat in conversations with Shepard. He often seeks guidance from Shepard due to a combination of his youth, lack of krogan guidance and his inexperience about the galaxy, having been educated solely by imprints from Okeer's tank. It takes a while for him to understand the images Okeer used to educate him with, but Grunt soon sees the funny side of killing turians and salarians, and is pleased with himself when he compiles his first list of enemies. Despite his violent nature, he respects Shepard's leadership, partly because Shepard faces great battles and has powerful enemies. If Grunt becomes loyal, he calls Shepard his battlemaster, as the Commander "has no equal".

Okeer's Legacy on Korlus. 2185, after Freedom's Progress Jedore's Blue Suns camp and Okeer's cloning lab on Korlus; then the Normandy On Korlus, Jedore, the Blue Suns garrison commander, harangues Shepard over loudspeakers while the squad fights through her mercs. A wounded merc, a compulsory encounter, gives up information about Okeer and the tank-bred krogan; Shepard can let him go, or kill him if he raises the alarm.

A veteran of the Krogan Rebellions fought more than a thousand years ago, Okeer is a militant radical who was so ruthless and fanatical that even his own people turned on him. He maintains an extreme social Darwinist belief that the effect it has had on krogan natural selection, rather than the loss of numbers, is where the genophage has performed its greatest damage. His efforts aren't geared toward curing it, but rather, toward ignoring it completely in the goal of "perfecting" his species. With each rare newborn, even the weaker ones, cared for, grown to adulthood and possibly reproducing, Okeer believes the ancient krogan philosophy that only the strongest survive and reproduce is lost. He sees the survival of the weak and the integration of their genetics into the krogan gene pool as proof that krogan are growing weaker with each generation, becoming shadows of those who fought in the Rebellions. An army of krogan of equal or greater strength, skill, and wits as those of the Rebellions, even a limited and non\-reproducing one, will be enough to bring the galaxy to its knees. To this end Okeer experimented with genetics and sold a great number of his kind to the Collectors for the technology he required, earning himself a vile reputation among krogan and forcing him off Tuchanka. Offworld, Okeer found a sponsor willing to provide him resources. A Blue Suns commander named Jedore desired a mixed\-unit army composed of cloned krogan loyal to her with hired merc specialists leading the krogan shock troops. She set Okeer up with a facility on Korlus (with Rana Thanoptis as his assistant if she escaped Virmire) to breed new types of krogan in breeding tanks. Okeer gives Jedore exactly what she asked for: an army of strong, healthy krogan warriors. Jedore, and the Blue Suns mercenaries under her, complain that the krogan berserkers are uncontrollable, but Okeer could see the only problem was that she lacked the ability to command. The tank\-breds are then used by the Suns as targets in live\-fire exercises. Unbeknownst to Jedore, the army of krogan Okeer bred for her are mere rejects compared to one ultimate warrior "prototype" he has been perfecting. This particular prototype survived being imparted with Collector information, but only after Okeer learned how to do so without killing the test subject. When Commander Shepard comes to Okeer to recruit him for the fight against the Collectors, the latter is found in the middle of releasing his flawed test subjects en masse to kill Jedore's forces as a means to grant more time to finalize his greatest creation. Okeer reveals that he knows about the Commander's actions on Virmire and expresses his approval, stating bluntly that Saren's "pale horde" were not true krogan, and opines that numbers alone are meaningless. Once Jedore realizes Okeer has been doublecrossing the Suns, she releases a toxic gas via vents in the lab and calls a clean slate on the entire project. As the tech that went into the creation of Okeer's super soldier is irreplaceable, he bargains with Shepard to save it. He refuses to leave his creation and stays in the lab as Shepard runs off to kill Jedore. After the battle, the gases had already suffocated Okeer. He leaves a dying message to tell Shepard to take his super soldier (later taking the name of Grunt, after his last words) to defeat the Collectors. What knowledge of the Collectors Okeer had was destroyed with his death, though he did state in his dying declaration that if he knew of why the Collectors were kidnapping humans, he would have told Shepard. His super solder, Grunt, has blurry memories of Collector ships owing to the tech that went in his creation. Wrex expresses a dislike of Okeer if Shepard asks him, while Wreav considers the connection between Grunt and the krogan scientist a good reason to accept Grunt into Clan Urdnot. If Shepard kills the Thresher Maw and Gatatog Uvenk offers Grunt a place in Clan Gatatog, Grunt, in his disgust, refers to Okeer as his father. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

The krogan warlord Okeer has hired the Blue Suns to provide funding and security for him as he works on his experiment to create the "perfect" krogan, offering the rejects from his experiment as payment. A Blue Suns officer named Jedore is assigned to assess the potential of the rejects as viable shock troops. Okeer and Jedore quickly begin to lose patience with each other when the rejects prove too unstable to be reliable soldiers; Jedore begins to think that Okeer's project is not worth the time and money the Suns have invested, while Okeer considers Jedore to be an incompetent leader and chafes under her direction. The Blue Suns decide to use the unstable rejects for live ammo training, with Okeer giving them the impression that the next generation of tank\-grown krogan would benefit from an improved mental imprint that would make them more reliable. Eventually, Shepard arrives on Korlus looking for Okeer, who was believed to have valuable intel on the Collectors. Okeer uses the distraction caused by Shepard's arrival to release several of the rejects, which proceed to attack both Shepard's squad and the Blue Suns. Jedore quickly discovers this betrayal, and decides to kill Okeer and use his research to restart the project with a blank slate. By the time Shepard makes it to Okeer's lab, Jedore has holed up in a massive storage bay with the next generation of tank\-bred krogan. Although she has several of these tanks "flushed" with poison gas, she releases some of them to fight Shepard. Although Jedore does not survive the battle with Shepard, she does succeed in killing Okeer, who sacrificed himself to save his prized creation.

Jedore was a Blue Suns commander and a financial contributor to Okeer's krogan cloning project. She was tasked with evaluating the cloned krogan's combat effectiveness and determining whether they were suitable as shock troops. She was disappointed by the results, finding the clones crazed and uncontrollable and near useless as frontline troops. Okeer dismissed her complaints, attributing her lack of control over the krogan to her own inability to command.

Concluding that Okeer and his krogan were not worth the time and money invested, Jedore attempted to destroy both him and his creations. She was killed by Commander Shepard, who intervened on Okeer's dying wish to save the still-unawakened tank-bred krogan later named Grunt. Jedore was described as unstable, with a massive superiority complex and a hair-trigger temper; her ranting over the comm during Shepard's infiltration was severe enough that her own subordinates demanded she stop clogging the channel. In combat she carried an ML-77 Missile Launcher, had very strong shields, armor, and health, and used Tech Armor like other Blue Suns commanders. During the fight she activated four dormant Krogan Berserkers from their tanks one at a time and was supported by a YMIR Mech, and was highly susceptible to Stasis.

“I am pure krogan; you should be in awe.” **Grunt** is a genetically engineered krogan super soldier. Bred and educated in a tank, he was intended to exemplify the best traits of the krogan, and help reinvigorate his species. In the meantime, he fights alongside Commander Shepard to satisfy his natural desire for violence. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

|  | *This article is about the enemy type in Mass Effect 2\. For Grunt's class power, see Krogan Berserker (power).* *For the enemy type in Mass Effect: Andromeda, see Berserker.* | | --- | --- | |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | **Krogan Berserkers** are tank\-bred krogan created by the warlord Okeer. They were bred in an attempt to create "perfect krogan" \- krogan who lacked the genophage's genetic markers, and who lacked the "weak genes" bred into the krogan population as a result of nurturing every surviving newborn, no matter how feeble. While in their tanks, these krogan were shown images such as the vulnerable parts of alien anatomy and how best to take advantage of them, as well as past battles in an attempt to both prepare them for war and inspire hatred for Okeer's enemies. The krogan were also educated by what one berserker described as a 'voice' or 'scratching sound', which taught them how to speak, move and fight. The vast majority of Okeer's specimens were failures. These krogan were handed over to Blue Suns commander Jedore for her army, and Okeer kept the one specimen he considered perfect for himself. However, the Berserkers proved to be extremely violent with their main desire being to fight and kill. Deeming them uncontrollable, Jedore instead used them for live ammunition training for her Blue Suns mercs. They mature very quickly as one encountered by Shepard was only seven days old and fighting several Blue Suns mercenaries. Berserkers seem to be susceptible to blood rage, making them even harder to control.

Rana Thanoptis Under the Desk. 2183, the assault on Saren's base on Virmire Rana Thanoptis's office inside Saren's cloning and indoctrination facility Spared, she crosses Shepard's path again on Korlus in 2185 during the hunt for Dr. Okeer, now writing mind-imprint routines for his tank-bred krogan, most of whom die. She admits she shut off the facility's cameras when she saw Shepard approaching. Let go a second time, she quips that she "knows how Shepard works" and means to get well clear before anything blows up.

Krogan Berserkers were tank-bred krogan created by the warlord Okeer in his attempt to breed "perfect krogan" free of the genophage's genetic markers and of the "weak genes" he believed nurturing feeble newborns had spread through the species. While in their tanks the specimens were shown alien anatomical weak points and past battles to prepare them for war and instill hatred of Okeer's enemies, and were taught to speak, move and fight by what one Berserker called a "voice" or "scratching sound." Most specimens failed and were handed to Blue Suns commander Jedore for her army, while Okeer kept the single specimen he judged perfect, who became Grunt. The Berserkers proved uncontrollably violent, driven only to fight and kill, and were prone to blood rage, so Jedore used them as live-fire training targets for her mercenaries. They matured extremely fast; one Shepard encountered on Korlus was only seven days old.

As enemies on Korlus, Berserkers were ferocious in close quarters, armed with shotguns and the Carnage ability, constantly advancing and using a stunning charge. They had good armor and very fast health regeneration. Incinerate, Warp and incendiary or Warp Ammo stripped their armor and blocked regeneration; precise ranged weapons, sniper rifles and staying at distance were advised, and once disarmored they could be knocked off the area's narrow walkways to their deaths.

With Grunt in your party, speak with the current leader of Clan Urdnot, who is either Shepard's old friend, Wrex, or (if he died on Virmire or was never recruited) his brother, Wreav. Either will note that Grunt is not sick, he is of the age where he must complete the krogan Rite of Passage, and refers the party to the clan Shaman. The clan Shaman will relate various information about the rite, as well as krogan history and culture. Gatatog Uvenk will protest Grunt taking the Rite, as he is tank bred. You can get Uvenk to stand down in a number of ways. After Shepard agrees to be Grunt's krantt, the Shaman sends Grunt and company to the traditional grounds of the Rite.

Grunt's Rite of Passage. 2185, after Horizon, once Grunt is woken from his tank Tuchanka — Clan Urdnot's camp, then the Rite grounds The Urdnot leader explains Grunt is not sick, only of the age to take the Rite of Passage, and sends the party to the clan Shaman. Gatatog Uvenk, a traditionalist from the Urdnot border camp, protests loudly that Grunt is tank-bred and has no right to the Rite, going over the leader's head to appeal directly to the Shaman, who is plainly irritated by him. Uvenk withdraws his objection but warns he will settle the matter elsewhere.

She used her fertility to amass male followers, who competed with each other for the right to have children with her. evidence.text: Little is known about krogan language except for a few non\-translatable terms. Some terms are specific to certain krogan clans, such as "Aralakh", which was taken from Clan Raik. Known krogan words are listed below. - *Aralakh* \- "Eye of Wrath" - *hrakhor* \- pejorative, referring to unskilled henchmen by context - *korbal* \- roughly, "victory or death" - *krantt* \- a warrior's most trusted allies - *ru'shan* \- "Child of my Blood" - *ruzad* \- "judge" - *Trobror* \- "cinder" or "ash heap" Krogan names are composed of two parts, a clan name followed by a given name. At birth, krogan are identified by their given name only. A clan name is bestowed after krogan complete the rite of passage of the clan they wish to join. While krogan actions speak louder than words, linguistic quirks are not unknown to them. Known krogan idioms include "like a thresher maw pet", indicating something is unpredictable.

evidence.text:
Grunt: Rite of Passage was Grunt's loyalty mission in Mass Effect 2, available after Horizon once Grunt had been woken following Dossier: The Warlord. In the Normandy cargo hold, Grunt paced restlessly and told Shepard his desire to destroy and kill had become an involuntary compulsion; he asked to be taken to Tuchanka because EDI lacked krogan medical records, which the krogan fiercely guarded after the salarians used them to build the genophage.

On Tuchanka, Shepard spoke with the leader of Clan Urdnot, either Wrex or (if he died on Virmire or was never recruited) his brother Wreav, who explained that Grunt was not sick but of the age to undergo the krogan Rite of Passage, and referred the party to the clan Shaman. Gatatog Uvenk protested Grunt taking the Rite because he was tank-bred, but could be made to stand down. Shepard agreed to serve as Grunt's krantt and the Shaman sent the party to the traditional Rite grounds.

The Rite consisted of three waves triggered by activating a keystone: a swarm of varren, then fire-breathing klixen delivered by unkillable Harvesters, and finally a Thresher Maw that had to be survived for five minutes, with extra accolades for killing it. Killing the Maw earned the krogan's respect; it had not been done since Wrex's own Rite. Afterward Uvenk and his krantt appeared, offering to accept Grunt into Clan Gatatog as little more than a trophy; regardless of dialogue choice the encounter ended in a fight against Uvenk, who had barrier and armor, plus four Gatatog Warriors. Once they were defeated, the Shaman welcomed Grunt as a full member of Clan Urdnot and awarded a shotgun damage upgrade (Synchronized Pulsar), and Fortack's Database granted a discount. Grunt also unlocked the Fortification power. The Shaman later emailed Shepard demanding Grunt be kept alive for the krogan's survival. In Mass Effect 3, if this mission was not completed and Shepard spared the Rachni Queen during Attican Traverse: Krogan Team, Grunt would die.

evidence.text: Krogan are divided into numerous clans. Membership in a clan allows a krogan to own property, join the army and apply to serve under a battlemaster. Clan diplomats represent the strength of their people to other clans, and thus make it their job to look intimidating lest their clan be targeted for conquest. Young krogan undergo a rite of passage that is overseen by a shaman respective to the clan the krogan wishes to join. In Clan Urdnot, this rite consists of battling various wild fauna on Tuchanka, ending with an encounter with a thresher maw. Merely surviving for five minutes is considered proof of worthiness, but killing the thresher maw increases the initiate's prestige and standing. In Clan Nakmor, it's claimed that it isn't so much a rite of passage as a "death trip", and surviving entails membership into the clan. Few outsiders have seen a rite of passage take place, even though there are no rules in krogan tradition that state that a non\-krogan can't help with the undertaking of the rite by acting as the participant's krantt. Known krogan clans: - Clan Bragus \- Bragus Thul plays as a quarterback in North\-American\-Union\-Rules football. - Clan Dahmbra \- one of several clans with individuals that joined the Andromeda Initiative. - Clan Drau \- Drau Sorze is a "ruzad", or "judge", in the Republic of Ghurst on Tuchanka. - Clan Forsan \- this clan's leader declared being hit by pyjak dung is grounds for executing the trader responsible for introducing them to Tuchanka. - Clan Ganar \- Ganar Wrang, an exiled krogan battlemaster, founded the Blood Pack mercenary group. - Clan Gatatog \- led by Gatatog Uvenk on Tuchanka. - Clan Graken \- Graken Dhal, a warlord, involved in the bombardment of Digeris during the Krogan Rebellions. - Clan Gulnaz \- one of several clans with individuals that joined the Andromeda Initiative. - Clan Hailot \- clan leader Hailot Wrund controlled Garvug prior to the corporatist invasion in 2185\. - Clan Jair \- one of several clans with individuals that joined the Andromeda Initiative. - Clan Jorgal \- a clan known to have one of the longest krogan breeding lines and oldest bloodlines. - Clan Jurdon \- an enemy of Clan Urdnot on Tuchanka. - Clan Kariss \- one of several minor clans with individuals that joined the Andromeda Initiative. - Clan Khel \- Khel Burrum is a krogan competing at Pinnacle Station. - Clan Kohrr \- one of several clans with individuals that joined the Andromeda Initiative. - Clan Kormer \- one of several clans with individuals that joined the Andromeda Initiative. - Clan Korten \- a clan known for making klixen\-roasted varren jerky with their own signature pyjak sauce. - Clan Nakmor - Clan Quash \- Quash Hurgott is a Blood Pack commander. - Clan Raik \- source of the word "Aralakh", meaning "Eye of Wrath", which became the common name used by the galaxy to refer to Tuchanka's star. - Clan Ravanor \- the clan runs a mining operation on Tuchanka; Warlord Ravanor Tusk is a clan member. - Clan Shath \- Shath Norda survived a trip to the planet Kruban. - Clan Strogjaw \- Strogjaw Grog is a member who joined then deserted the Andromeda Initiative. - Clan Talyth \- a clan that attempted to rebuild a dreadnought on Tuchanka with the help of turian duarch Ellis Valterus. - Clan Thax \- the clan of krogan businessman Thax Vorak. - Clan Urdnot - Clan Weyrloc - Clan Wik \- one of several clans with individuals that joined the Andromeda Initiative.

evidence.text: |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | Uvenk resides in the Urdnot border camp, sticking close by the reiging clan leader. His traditionalist leanings have him voicing his opposition to the reformations initiated by Urdnot Wrex if he is the clan leader, claiming that they will only serve to weaken the krogan as a whole. On the other hand, if Urdnot Wreav is the clan leader, Uvenk is much more deferential and supportive of his chief's conservative stance. When Commander Shepard accompanies Grunt to complete his Rite of Passage, Uvenk insults Grunt for his status as a tank\-bred krogan and vehemently opposes allowing him to join the ranks of Urdnot. When the Urdnot leader indicates preference for sending Grunt to the Rite, Uvenk tries to go around them and speak directly to the Urdnot Shaman, though his protests against allowing Grunt to undertake the Rite are met with irritation by the venerable Shaman. Shepard is able to make Uvenk back down after proving to the Shaman that they will support Grunt as his krantt, either by humbling Uvenk with words or answering his insults with a headbutt in the typical krogan fashion. Uvenk resentfully withdraws his denial for Grunt's Rite for the moment but threatens to settle the matter elsewhere. Shortly after the third and final battle of the Rite, a shuttle carrying Uvenk and several Gatatog Warriors arrives. If Shepard and Grunt completed the Rite of Passage by killing the Thresher Maw, Uvenk acknowledges the unquestionable proof of Grunt's strength and reveals his plan to convince Grunt to join Clan Gatatog, albeit as a trophy and in\-name\-only member, solely in order to increase Uvenk's own stature. Conversely, if the Rite was finished by surviving the Thresher Maw's attack without killing it, Uvenk merely tells Grunt that he is not worthy of joining a clan because he is impure. If Uvenk tries to recruit Grunt, his cynical overtures are violently rebuffed by Grunt, who has no interest in being used as a tool while having his identity, his krantt, and his lineage disrespected. Either way, a battle with the Gatatog warriors and Uvenk ensues which ends in their deaths. On the Normandy afterward, Grunt expresses his thanks to Shepard and his satisfaction at Uvenk's demise.

evidence.text: Thresher Maw! This is not so much a wave as it is a giant creature attack. There is only one Thresher Maw and the primary objective is simply to survive. All you have to do is survive the attack for five minutes and the test will be ended, though there are additional dialogue accolades if you succeed in taking it down. If you manage to kill the Thresher Maw, you gain the respect of the krogan and the Rite ends. The Thresher Maw moves around the outskirts of the map, but its trail of flying dirt clods is easy to follow when it dives back underground. The Thresher Maw can destroy the "merely metal" structures, so try to avoid those for cover and go for the sturdier stone/concrete pillars and walls instead. Its acid spit is an area of effect attack and will accurately shoot at you even if you're cloaked. The blue tongue is **not** a weak spot—shooting it does not cause any additional damage. **Combat Strategy:** There is one indestructible stone pillar on the low ground area of the level—to the right as you face out from the keystone—that you can use to take cover from the Maw from any direction it might appear. Additionally, there are two respawning thermal clips at the base of this pillar as well as easy access to a medi\-gel and power cells on the higher ground that you can pick up from the edge of the raised area without needing to climb up. This is without a doubt the optimal place to fight the Maw, as all other locations will involve considerable running about when the Maw moves. Place your squadmates in cover behind the other two indestructible pillars on the high ground and they should also be safe and might even draw the Maw's fire giving you free rein. If a squadmate does go down it's not the end of the world: Shepard alone is more than enough to beat the Maw even on Insanity. **Combat Tips:** - The metal pillars can be destroyed by the Thresher Maw in one hit, but any cover made of stone/concrete is not destructible. You should always try to interpose indestructible cover between yourself and the Maw. The Maw's spit projectile does have an area of effect so try to be as completely in cover as possible when the Maw attacks to ensure you are not hit. - Shepard's shields take longer than usual to recover after an acid hit, so be careful. On the plus side it takes about three consecutive hits to kill Shepard even on Insanity. Don't hesitate to use a medi\-gel to quickly restore your shields (provided you have the Emergency Shielding medi\-gel upgrade). - A well\-upgraded heavy pistol is more than sufficient to take out the Maw as long as you take advantage of respawning thermal clips to keep replenishing its ammo. - On Insanity, the Thresher Maw's sheer amount of health makes using heavy weapons inefficient. Conventional weapons modded with anti\-armor ammo powers are your best bet. - Though nominally ineffective against armor, Grunt's Concussive Shot can still "stagger" the Maw, reducing the number of acid shots it will take before retreating. - Zaeed's Inferno Grenade, Mordin's Incinerate, and Samara's Reave are examples of good squadmate attacks to use. Using weapons with high armor penetration such as the Widow, M\-76 Revenant, M\-96 Mattock, or most pistols will help a lot. - The Cain will usually only damage half the Thresher Maw's health on Insanity. - The Thresher Maw is immune to the effects of Stasis.

evidence.text:
Gatatog Uvenk was a krogan battlemaster and leader of Clan Gatatog on Tuchanka in 2185. A traditionalist who championed the warrior culture that drove the Krogan Rebellions, he believed Clan Gatatog stood at a turning point between renewed power and glory or fading into history, and so allied his people with the dominant Clan Urdnot to curry favor with its leader. He resided at the Urdnot border camp. If Urdnot Wrex led the clan, Uvenk openly opposed his reforms as weakening the krogan; if Urdnot Wreav led, Uvenk was deferential and supportive.

When Commander Shepard accompanied Grunt to complete his Rite of Passage, Uvenk insulted Grunt as a tank-bred krogan and opposed his joining Urdnot, appealing directly to the Urdnot Shaman, who was irritated by his protests. Shepard made Uvenk back down by proving the team would serve as Grunt's krantt, either humbling him with words or answering with a headbutt; Uvenk withdrew his objection but vowed to settle the matter elsewhere. After the final battle of the Rite, Uvenk arrived by shuttle with several Gatatog Warriors. If Grunt had killed the thresher maw, Uvenk acknowledged his strength and offered him in-name-only membership in Clan Gatatog as a trophy to boost Uvenk's own stature; if the maw was merely survived, Uvenk dismissed Grunt as impure. Grunt violently rejected the offer, and a battle ensued that ended in the deaths of Uvenk and his warriors. Grunt afterward thanked Shepard and expressed satisfaction at Uvenk's death. Uvenk said: "Aliens don't know strength. My followers are true krogan. Everything about Grunt is a lie." In combat he hung back using Warp while his warriors charged, wielding an M-300 Claymore heavy shotgun, a biotic Barrier, and armor. He wore modified Battlemaster Armor from the Geth Armory and was voiced by Michael Dorn.

evidence.text:
Thresher maws were enormous subterranean carnivores that spent their lives eating or hunting for food, bursting from the ground without warning when disturbed. They reproduced via spores that could lie dormant for millennia and survive deep space and atmospheric re-entry, so maw spores appeared on many worlds, spread by earlier generations of space travelers, possibly predating the asari.

They lived alone in large underground nests, growing over 30 meters above ground with a body nearly twice that size beneath the surface; an adult's body never fully left the ground, with only the head and tentacles erupting to attack. They fed through an unusual photosynthesis using absorbed solar radiation plus minerals and ores consumed from the ground, favoring bodies with little or no atmosphere. Mostly immobile above ground, they moved at high speed while burrowing, absorbed tremendous damage, and attacked by spitting viscous acid, bursting up beneath prey, and smashing targets with their claws while emitting infrasound. Shields were completely ineffective against them.

The Alliance first encountered thresher maws on the colony of Akuze in 2177, where they killed nearly an entire marine rescue force. If Shepard has the Sole Survivor background, Shepard alone survived; Corporal Toombs, met later on Ontarom, claimed Cerberus deliberately caused the Akuze massacre to study the maws and held him captive for experiments, and Cerberus later used the same tactic to lure Admiral Kahoku's team into a nest on Edolus. Maws are found on many uncharted worlds, usually one per planet, including Antibaar, Chohe, Nepheron, Nonuel, Presrop, Xawin, Trebin and Edolus.

In Mass Effect 2, a thresher maw is the final test of Clan Urdnot's Rite of Passage on Tuchanka, lured to the proving grounds by ground-pounding pistons to attack Grunt's krantt. Gatatog Uvenk notes that the last krogan to kill a maw on foot was Urdnot Wrex. In Mass Effect 3, Kalros, a legendary maw called "the mother from which all other thresher maws spawn" and the largest ever seen, roams Tuchanka near the Shroud facility. Shepard activates two maw hammers to summon her against a Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud; she coils around it and drags it underground. Her size prompts Javik to remark that maws are now too big to ride, implying they were smaller in Prothean times. The concept was confirmed by art director Derek Watts to draw on Dune's sandworms, and also resembles D&D Ankhegs, the Star Wars Sarlacc, and the real Bobbit worm.

evidence.text:
This page collects gameplay information and combat tactics for fighting thresher maws as enemy units in Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2, as opposed to the general lore page.

In Mass Effect, thresher maws appear on uncharted worlds and can be fought in the Mako or on foot. Their nests are identifiable by a roughly 50–75 meter circular area of flat ground with low hills and shallow pits; maws only surface on the flat portions and retreat underground if the player leaves the circle for about five seconds. The page stresses never driving into or meleeing a maw, since its claws can cause instant death, and that its acid spit bypasses shields entirely and can destroy the Mako or kill Shepard in one hit. Recommended tactics include keeping distance, circle-strafing or using the Mako's boosters to hop over each acid projectile while firing, and using cover behind hills. A quirk let players kill the same maw twice for double experience by killing it before its health bar appeared. In the Legendary Edition, maws spit a spread of acid balls that lead the target, stay underground longer with a visible dirt trail, and can deploy immobile Sensory Tentacles; killing in the Mako no longer carries an experience penalty, and maws do not heal when the player withdraws.

In Mass Effect 2, a single thresher maw must be fought on foot by Grunt and his krantt during Clan Urdnot's Rite of Passage on Tuchanka. It stays outside the playable area, lobbing fast high-damage acid blobs that delay shield and health regeneration, and periodically dives and tunnels to a new position. It has heavy armor with no weak points (the blue tongue and mouth take no bonus damage) and is immune to Stasis. Effective options include Warp, Reave and Incinerate against its armor, stone pillars for cover, well-upgraded heavy pistols such as the M-5 Phalanx or M-6 Carnifex, upgraded sniper rifles, and heavy weapons like the M-920 Cain or Collector Particle Beam.

The Normandy travels to Utukku, where Shepard meets Aralakh Company, an elite krogan unit led by Grunt — or, if Grunt died in the Mass Effect 2 suicide mission or was never released from his tank, by Urdnot Dagg.

**Urdnot Dagg** is a krogan who leads Aralakh Company if Grunt didn't survive the suicide mission or was never released from his tank. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | Either Urdnot Wrex or Urdnot Wreav chooses Urdnot Dagg to lead Aralakh Company. Dagg leads Aralakh Company on a mission to investigate a missing krogan scout team on Utukku, with assistance from Commander Shepard. When Dagg first meets Shepard, he expresses both admiration and jealousy that Shepard has the Reapers as enemies, wondering what the Commander must have done to earn such a reputation. If Shepard answers that Dagg also came highly recommended, Dagg will reveal that the reason he was chosen as leader is because he is a respected and feared soldier who his superiors believed would help Aralakh Company achieve greater unity. Dagg knows his company, boasting that every krogan under his command wants blood; if Shepard is female and quips that she will try to leave some for them, Dagg barks approvingly that "the female has bite!" Like most krogan, Dagg is eager for action, so much so that when Shepard first falls into the nest to begin the mission, Dagg assumes the Commander was intentionally charging into battle. However, at a moment when Shepard's squad can personally observe Aralakh Company battling rachni, Dagg has more trouble than Grunt would in his place, pinned down and unable to break cover. Dagg later sacrifices himself, fending off a swarm of Ravagers to buy time for Commander Shepard's squad to escape. Unlike Grunt, there is no way to save Dagg; whether Shepard chooses to save Aralakh Company or the Rachni Queen/Breeder, Dagg will always die from being overwhelmed by Ravagers.

Urdnot Dagg was a krogan soldier who led Aralakh Company during the Reaper War if Grunt did not survive the Collector base suicide mission or was never released from his tank. Either Urdnot Wrex or Urdnot Wreav, as leader of Clan Urdnot, chose Dagg to command the company because he was a respected and feared soldier whom his superiors believed would bring greater unity to Aralakh Company.

In 2186 Dagg led Aralakh Company on a mission to Utukku to investigate a missing krogan scout team, assisted by Commander Shepard. On first meeting Shepard, Dagg expressed both admiration and jealousy that Shepard had the Reapers as enemies, wondering what the Commander had done to earn such a reputation; if Shepard replied that Dagg came highly recommended, he explained his selection as leader. He boasted that every krogan under his command wanted blood, and if a female Shepard quipped she would leave some for them, he barked approvingly that "the female has bite!" Eager for battle, Dagg assumed Shepard was intentionally charging into combat when the Commander first fell into the rachni nest. During a moment when Shepard's squad could observe Aralakh Company fighting rachni, Dagg had more trouble than Grunt would have, pinned down and unable to break cover.

Dagg later sacrificed himself, fending off a swarm of Ravagers to buy time for Shepard's squad to escape. Unlike Grunt, there was no way to save Dagg; whether Shepard chose to save Aralakh Company or the Rachni Queen/Breeder, Dagg always died, overwhelmed by Ravagers.

“I don't need luck; I have ammo.” Grunt returns to fight the Reapers, provided he was released from his tank aboard the Normandy and survived the attack on the Collector base. He has since earned the command of Aralakh Company. The Urdnot chief notes that as a result, Aralakh Company is his best unit. If Wrex is alive, he put Grunt in charge because he exemplifies the bright future of the krogan, something Wrex hopes for his people; Grunt, as such, is optimistic and cares about his company more. If Wreav replaced Wrex, he put Grunt in charge for his strength; Grunt is also more blasé about his appointment, stating that it doesn't really matter to him as long as he gets to fight tough enemies. To a lesser extent, he still experiences the stigma of being tank\-born, rather than earning strength in the way other krogan feel is true. Nonetheless, his undeniable prowess in battle has earned him his place in the company. He helps Shepard investigate the disappearance of other squads in the tunnels of Utukku, where they discover a new brood of rachni who have been twisted by Reaper technology. If Shepard chooses to spare the Rachni Queen or artificial queen, Aralakh Company is left behind to cover her escape, much to Grunt's disgust; they are slaughtered holding off wave after wave of rachni, but the queen survives, providing rachni support. If not, Grunt gives the order to retreat, telling Aralakh Company to "get \[their] asses back to the shuttle"; this secures their escape, at the cost of the queen's life and any chance of rachni contribution to the war. Either way, Grunt breaks through a wall in the cavern to reach Shepard's squad, then runs with them back to the waiting shuttle. Realising the Reaper\-modified rachni are closing in on them, Grunt personally holds several Ravagers and Swarmers off to cover the Commander's escape. If Shepard chose to spare either queen, Grunt dies if his loyalty wasn't secured prior to the suicide mission. If Shepard chose to abandon either queen, Grunt survives regardless of his prior loyalty, limping out of the rachni nest all bloody and asking for something to eat. If Grunt died on Utukku, reactions from people who knew about him run the gamut from indifferent (Wreav) to forlorn (Garrus, Tali, Ashley, Wrex) to solemn wisecracking (Joker). If Grunt survived, he contributes to the war effort after recuperating from his "scratches". He passes along an additional message from Aralakh Company if Shepard chose to abandon the Utukku queen. **No Subject** --- From: Grunt THas a goood fight ShUpurd. You cant hear em but I;ve goht ARLlakh co,mpany chantin SHEPAR SHEPAR your name you know. as we down some ryNCOL to heal my woundS^\&!!( ryCNol! Whear are yOu? SHEPERD S HEPAURD  SHEPARUD!!! Shepard has a chance to speak to him on Earth prior to the final push at the final battle. Grunt then thanks the Commander for getting him out of the tank in the first place. If Grunt survived, the Genophage was cured, and organics and synthetics weren't merged at the conclusion of the war, he and Urdnot Wrex (if Wrex survived Virmire) are shown to be welcomed back at Tuchanka, heroes among a horde of cheering krogan. If Grunt did not survive the suicide mission or was never freed from his tank, his role is filled by Urdnot Dagg.

This was a Mass Effect 3 mission acquired automatically on returning from Priority: Sur'Kesh. The Urdnot clan leader, either Urdnot Wrex or Urdnot Wreav, reported that a krogan scouting team had gone missing while investigating rumors of activity at the rachni relay beyond it; speaking to him in the War Room changed the journal entry title to Attican Traverse: The Rachni. The Normandy received the team's last-known coordinates and Commander Shepard travelled to the planet Utukku in the Mulla Xul system of the Ninmah Cluster.

There Shepard met Aralakh Company, an elite krogan unit led by Grunt or, if Grunt had died in the Mass Effect 2 suicide mission or was never released from his tank, by Urdnot Dagg. Descending into tunnels beneath the surface, Shepard's team found the bodies of krogan scouts and discovered that the Reapers had established a breeding operation, using rachni to grow a biological army of Ravagers, Swarmers, and other troops. The mission featured heavy use of the M-451 Firestorm flamethrower against Reaper webbing, spore pods, gestation pods, Barrier Engines, and Reaper Nodes, and fights against Ravagers, Husks, and Cannibals.

At the central chamber Shepard confronted either the original Rachni Queen from Noveria, if she had been spared in Mass Effect, or the Breeder, a genetically revived rachni created by the Reapers. Shepard could leave her to die or help her escape on the condition she aid the war effort. Rescuing her required ordering Aralakh Company into a suicidal holding action: sparing the original Queen cost Aralakh Company 25 war asset points but gained 100 points of rachni workers, while rescuing the Breeder gave similar initial gains but the Breeder later betrayed the effort after Priority: Horizon, removing her asset and subtracting 100 points from the Alliance Engineering Corps. Leaving the rachni to die granted Aralakh Company as a 25-point war asset. Regardless of the choice, Grunt or Dagg stayed behind to hold off Ravagers so Shepard's party could reach the shuttle; Dagg always died, and Grunt died only if he had been disloyal in the previous game. In Legendary Edition, rescuing either the Queen or the Breeder meant Aralakh Company was not acquired at all. Afterward Garrus recounted rachni stories to Ensign Copeland in the Port Observation Lounge, and if aboard, Diana Allers discussed the scoop with Specialist Traynor.

If Grunt survives to become leader of Aralakh Company, he mentions that Okeer took steps to ensure he knew about the rachni. Apparently, Okeer respected the rachni as worthy enemies, and passed this respect on to his creation. |  | ***“Make no mistake — this is a one\-way trip.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Andromeda** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

If you saved the Rachni Queen in Mass Effect, you will speak to her during this cutscene. If not, you will converse with the Breeder, a genetically revived rachni created by the Reapers to serve as a progenitor for their biological army. Either way, you may choose to either leave her or help her to survive on the condition that she will assist in the fight against the Reapers. Your decision will not affect the Reapers' supply of Ravagers one way or another, be prepared to meet them in future battles. Your squadmates will argue for leaving the Queen/Breeder to die at the hands of her indoctrinated offspring, and they express skepticism at your decision no matter what it is. The leader of Aralakh company will also interject via radio and make clear that assisting the Queen/Breeder to escape would require ordering the krogan to make a suicidal last stand holding their positions against the Ravager hordes. - If you leave the rachni to die, you will gain Aralakh Company as a war asset worth 25 points, but no rachni assets. - If you choose to rescue the original queen from Noveria, Aralakh Company will suffer grievous losses in the holding action, reducing their strength by 25 points. However, the Queen provides rachni workers worth 100 points. - If you choose to rescue the new Breeder, initial war assets adjust as with saving the original queen; however, the Breeder proves untrustworthy after Priority: Horizon, simultaneously removing her war asset and subtracting 100 points from the Alliance Engineering Corps. No matter what you chose with the Rachni Queen/Breeder, Grunt or Urdnot Dagg will stay behind to hold off Ravagers while Shepard's party runs for the shuttle. Dagg will not survive this. Grunt will only die defending your escape if he was disloyal in the previous game (he will mention his outsider status in his dialogue outside the falling prefab in this case). If you completed Grunt's loyalty mission in the previous game, he will survive. Grunt adds 25 points to Aralakh Company's war asset as its leader if he survives the mission and an additional 25 points as representative of Clan Urdnot should you have earned his loyalty. Additionally, he will himself be added as an independent war asset worth 25 points. **Legendary Edition:** Should you rescue either the queen or the Breeder, Aralakh Company will not be acquired at all, regardless of Grunt's status.

**Ryncol** is an extremely potent liquor created by the krogan. Its exact composition is unknown, but it is clearly a very strong drink, given that it is created by and for the krogan. Grunt comments that ryncol "hits aliens like ground glass." Humans can survive drinking ryncol, although it is apparently unsafe for volus. One obtainable datapad contains a complaint made by a pirate about how the YMIR Mech he purchased "leaks \[fuel] like a volus after a mug of ryncol." When Commander Shepard visits the Dark Star Lounge and asks the bartender for five consecutive drinks, the Commander will be given a glass of ryncol. The bartender jokes that Shepard will "set off radiological alarms" after they drink it. Elcor and quarians can also survive drinking ryncol, although in case of the latter one must take immuno\-supplements and anti\-virals for weeks before attempting even one shot. In quarians it apparently makes them feel like "stained glass", and feels like "sipping knives" during the act itself. However, ancient quarians were capable of imbibing ryncol without issue since their immune systems weren't ruined yet by Migrant Fleet living. Ryncol apparently has "pure" and cocktail variants. It can be sold in 190 proof bottles. The turian bartender in the Dark Star Lounge creates a green ryncol mix served to Shepard by mixing separate components together. As per his prediction, it does indeed knock Shepard out, leading to a short sequence where the Commander groggily wakes up on the floor of the Dark Star's bathroom. In Jack's opinion, Shepard's stash of creme de menthe in the Personal Apartment can sicken people more than a sample of pure ryncol. Ryncol is also highly flammable: while on Silversun Strip, Grunt narrates to Shepard that he in fact used it as a Molotov cocktail merely by throwing a regular bottle at a C\-Sec aircar. Ryncol is highly acidic, capable of melting through machinery. Vomit from ryncol consumption is apparently purplish in color.

The page catalogs beverages consumed across the Mass Effect galaxies, spanning sustenance, personal preference and social lubrication. It lists dozens of named drinks with their species associations, effects and in-game contexts rather than telling a single story.

Alcoholic entries include Akantha, a popular asari liquor with a smoky flavor that cuts hangovers; asari honey mead, brewed in an Ardat-Yakshi monastery and the most expensive liquor in Aria T'Loak's bar; batarian ale, a potent green drink; Serrice Ice Brandy, a 1,000-credit favorite of Dr. Chakwas; turian brandy, which Tali'Zorah drinks through an "emergency induction port" (a straw); Elasa, a Thessian drink nicknamed "Sorrow's Companion" that Anderson drank in Chora's Den during his 2165 divorce; horosk, a hard turian drink strong enough to induce comas; ryncol, an extremely potent krogan liquor; and Noverian Rum, which Aria lamented being unable to obtain. Species-specific intoxicants include the hanar's mindfish (a hallucinogenic skin oil), the angaran marljeh and tavum, the volus bina, and krogan drinks such as burukh, sovak juice (used to name newborns via belching contests) and "liquefied turian," a reverse-chirality dare drink with adverse effects on all who tried it. Methanol is safely ingested by some species and mined by Terminus pirates on Antirumgon.

Cocktails feature heavily, many mixed by Samantha Traynor during Shepard's Citadel party using her college bartending knowledge: the Full Biotic Kick, Quad Kicker, Tasty Tankard, Frozen Pyjak (made from a bartender's spill pad and ice), Perfection, and the Weeping Heart (a martini with mild drell-skin venom). Umi Henon's concoctions in Andromeda, including Combat Juice and an angaran wine and ryncol mix, caused blackouts and wild dancing in Ryder. The Vortex on the Nexus served the Dirty Squirrel, Lucky Leprechaun, Tall Moose and Rotten Scoundrel via bartender Dutch Smith.

Non-alcoholic entries include coffee, credited by SAM for its own existence through Alec Ryder's consumption; soda; and sports drinks Tupari (with an aggressive marketing campaign claiming it revives ancestors) and its rival Paragade. Wine entries cover champagne, Thessia Red (the Illusive Man ordering a "'47"), and various bottles Anderson purchased. Whiskeys named include Mount Milgrom scotch, one 645-year-old bottle of which reached Andromeda and could be stolen by Reyes Vidal from Sloane Kelly's storeroom. Mass Effect: The Official Cocktail Book (2024) collects real-world recipes for many of these drinks.

"Omega: Batarian Bartender" was an assignment in Mass Effect 2, available after Freedom's Progress once Commander Shepard had access to Omega. It began by asking the bartender in the lower area of the Afterlife nightclub for a drink and choosing to buy one.

The batarian bartender, Forvan, served Shepard a drink that caused the Commander to fall unconscious; squadmates commented on this on waking. A passerby named Henner then explained that Forvan held a personal bias against humans after an incident in which several batarians were killed, and had been poisoning drinks served to humans in revenge.

Shepard could confront Forvan with several outcomes. Shepard could simply leave. With a high Renegade score, Shepard could force Forvan to drink his own poisoned drink, causing him to collapse. With a high Paragon score, Shepard could incite the crowd; Forvan would deny the allegations, draw a gun on Shepard, and be shot dead by a turian patron named Ogrinn. Shepard could also tell Forvan he was finished poisoning people, then still use Charm or Intimidate, or finally tell him he was not worth the trouble, letting him run away for Paragon points.

Regardless of resolution, Forvan was replaced by a salarian bartender who served Shepard free drinks on future visits to Afterlife. The assignment rewarded 40 (50) experience. It was internally referred to as "(Omega:) Bekke."

"Silver Coast Casino: Infiltration" was a Mass Effect 3 Citadel DLC mission following Citadel: Identity Theft I. Arms dealer Elijah Khan was hosting a charity gala at his casino, and Shepard worked with Maya Brooks to bypass security and reach his panic room. The mission involved no combat: Brooks crawled through a ventilation shaft while Shepard, accompanied by any squadmate except EDI (barred as an AI/mech), mingled with guests and, on cue, distracted patrolling guards and cameras. Using resonance emitter lenses provided by Liara (which turned Shepard's eyes yellow), Shepard followed colored underground circuits, bypassed junction boxes, pressure pads, and camera boxes, and raised the security threat level if seen acting suspiciously, with critical mission failure if caught outright. Two ATMs could be hacked for 3,000 credits each.

After Brooks was briefly caught near the panic room and Shepard intercepted a guard to call it a false alarm, the team entered the safe room to find Khan already dead. Brooks accessed his terminal and found a deletion order; Shepard noticed the comm had not been wiped and activated it, bringing up a face distorted beyond recognition by signal degradation. The figure vowed to take everything Shepard was and owned before cutting the call, which Brooks could not trace. Shepard ordered the drives pulled for EDI to analyze. Rewards totaled roughly 30,000 credits including Alliance funding.

The page collects the casino's "mingle" dialogue with named guests. Representative lines:

Rolan Quarn, a barefaced turian con artist loitering by Khan's gate: "Con men leave their marks angry. Con artists leave them smiling."

Rolan Quarn, assessing Khan for Shepard: "He's ruthless and rich, but not very bright. Temperamental. Doesn't deal well with the unexpected."

Jonah Ashland, of Eldfell-Ashland Energy, drinking after losing income to Reaper attacks on helium-3 facilities: "Young people party. I drink. Tonight it's ryncol on the rocks."

Eve's Funeral at the Hollows. 2186, Tuchanka, after Priority: Tuchanka, if Maelon's data was destroyed the Hollows, the sacred krogan burial ground on Tuchanka Eve's body was brought to the center of the Hollows and incinerated in a funeral pyre—a krogan tradition reserved for those who died particularly valorous deaths, such as those who saved the future of the entire race. Eve's eulogy was given by the Urdnot Shaman, the keeper of krogan rites and traditions.

Krogan tradition is steeped in ritual. When a krogan is born, he suffers the **Rite of Life**. When he comes of age, he undergoes the **Rite of Passage**. If he wishes to be considered for breeding, he must take the **Rite of Honor**. When facing a new enemy, the **Rite of Firsts** is invoked. If two krogan are quarreling with each other, the **Rite of Union** may serve as a way to heal the bond between them by giving the pair a mutual enemy to fight. If one wishes to take over clan leadership, the **Rite of Authority** determines whether the current leader keeps his post or loses it to the challenger. Positions of power also bear the responsibility of more rites, like being clan leader or shaman. The Rite of Passage and all other rites and traditions are preserved by the clan shaman. A shaman can be of either gender: they must undergo lengthy and torturous rites to assume the position, and is required to give up their name. Because of this level of commitment, the shaman is one of the most respected members of a clan. The krogan have at least two ways of formally dealing with their dead. Suicides are left for scavengers to feed upon. Another is via funeral pyre, where the shaman eulogizes the dead and symbolically consigns it to the Void. Known instances of the pyre include krogan who have died a particularly valorous death, e.g. by saving the future of the entire race.

The Shaman was a krogan living at the Urdnot Camp on Tuchanka who was in charge of Clan Urdnot's rites. Despite being responsible for keeping krogan traditions alive, he was irritated by the ostensibly traditionalist Gatatog Uvenk's objections to the tank-bred Grunt, and allowed Grunt to perform the Rite of Passage over Uvenk's protests.

If Commander Shepard taunted Uvenk for using politics instead of fighting, the Shaman praised the Commander for undermining Uvenk with words, Uvenk's "natural weapon"; if Shepard headbutted Uvenk in krogan fashion, the Shaman was particularly amused, judging that the Commander understood krogan ideals better than "those who whine like pups." Afterward the Shaman told Shepard he had gone through many rites to become shaman, including giving up his name, that those rites were so physically and mentally torturous they made him wish he were dead, and that further rites had to be performed every dawn and dusk. Grunt, if present, called the job terrible, and the Shaman agreed. Shepard could also return to tell him stories of past battles against worthy foes, including stopping Saren and a Reaper at the Citadel; the Shaman knew of and respected Spectre combat prowess.

In Mass Effect 3, if Eve died during the mission to cure the genophage, the Shaman delivered the eulogy at her funeral. A separate multiplayer class, the Krogan Shaman Adept, is unrelated to this character.

Eve's Funeral at the Hollows. 2186, Tuchanka, after Priority: Tuchanka, if Maelon's data was destroyed the Hollows, the sacred krogan burial ground on Tuchanka If Shepard destroyed Maelon's data during Mass Effect 2, Eve died of complications from having incomplete data during the genophage cure procedure on Tuchanka, regardless of whether Shepard sabotaged the cure or not. This caused several krogan clans to fall into conflict over who was responsible for her death, weakening krogan forces as a whole. The krogan held a funeral for her at the Hollows, the sacred krogan burial ground, attended by many krogan, the Urdnot leader (either Wrex or Wreav), and Shepard.

Eventually, the salarian doctor declares Eve ready for travel to Tuchanka. After the genophage cure is prepared, Shepard arrives on Tuchanka and the krogan prepare to use the Shroud to spread the cure. A confrontation ensues at the Hollows, the sacred burial ground of the krogan, when some of the krogan clans became hostile on seeing a salarian involved in the operation. The potential fight is averted when Eve delivers a speech that they must put aside their differences and fight together against the Reapers. In a joint operation with the turians to attack a Destroyer guarding the Shroud, the krogan led by Clan Urdnot leave the camp in Tomkahs. However, the operation goes wrong as the krogan get off to a late start, and the turians end up with a solitary airstrike where they are outmatched. The convoy then comes under attack and Shepard orders them to move out and leave the squad behind. After Shepard manages to fight through the ruins and back to the convoy, Eve proposes an idea to eliminate the Reaper. She mentions that the Shroud is near the two largest Maw Hammers in existence, and they can summon Kalros, "The Mother of all Thresher Maws". Eve says that Tuchanka is as much her home as it is the krogans', so if the hammers are activated, then she will come. While the maw has the Reaper distracted, the salarian scientist can finish the cure. As Shepard sets off, Eve heads into a nearby lab with her salarian doctor to finish the cure. If the Commander saved Maelon's data, then Eve survives the procedure to cure the genophage, and Shepard later gains strong support from the krogan clans. At the conclusion of the mission, Eve finally reveals her birth name to the Commander and says that they will always be friends. She later sends a message to Shepard, informing the Commander of the various krogan clans gathering in the Kelphic Valley, to whom she promises to speak to ensure that genophage cure isn't taken for granted. If Shepard chose to destroy Maelon's data back in 2185, however, Eve dies due to complications from having incomplete data, regardless of whether Shepard sabotaged the genophage cure or not. This causes several krogan clans to fall into conflict over who was responsible for Eve's death, weakening them as a whole. The krogan hold a funeral for her, attended by many krogan, the Urdnot leader, as well as Shepard. Her body is brought to the center of the Hollows, incinerated in a funeral pyre. Eve's eulogy is given by the current Urdnot shaman. Even if the genophage is dealt with, Eve may still die later, if Shepard does not aid Lieutenant Victus in disarming a rearmed turian bomb left over from the Krogan Rebellions. Eve was rallying the clans in the Kelphic Valley when the bomb explodes, obliterating her and the krogan population present. Shepard shortly receives a message from the Urdnot leader stating she died.
